instruction:
Create specification files that define WHAT the system should do.

Create one spec file per capability listed in the proposal's Capabilities section.
- New capabilities: use the exact kebab-case name from the proposal (specs/<capability>/spec.md).
- Modified capabilities: use the existing spec folder name from openspec/specs/<capability>/ when creating the delta spec at specs/<capability>/spec.md.

Delta operations (use ## headers):
- **ADDED Requirements**: New capabilities
- **MODIFIED Requirements**: Changed behavior - MUST include full updated content
- **REMOVED Requirements**: Deprecated features - MUST include **Reason** and **Migration**
- **RENAMED Requirements**: Name changes only - use FROM:/TO: format

Format requirements:
- Each requirement: `### Requirement: <name>` followed by description
- Use SHALL/MUST for normative requirements (avoid should/may)
- Each scenario: `#### Scenario: <name>` with WHEN/THEN format
- **CRITICAL**: Scenarios MUST use exactly 4 hashtags (`####`). Using 3 hashtags or bullets will fail silently.
- Every requirement MUST have at least one scenario.

MODIFIED requirements workflow:
1. Locate the existing requirement in openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md
2. Copy the ENTIRE requirement block (from `### Requirement:` through all scenarios)
3. Paste under `## MODIFIED Requirements` and edit to reflect new behavior
4. Ensure header text matches exactly (whitespace-insensitive)

Common pitfall: Using MODIFIED with partial content loses detail at archive time.
If adding new concerns without changing existing behavior, use ADDED instead.

Example:
```
## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: User can export data
The system SHALL allow users to export their data in CSV format.

#### Scenario: Successful export
- **WHEN** user clicks "Export" button
- **THEN** system downloads a CSV file with all user data

## REMOVED Requirements

### Requirement: Legacy export
**Reason**: Replaced by new export system
**Migration**: Use new export endpoint at /api/v2/export
```

Specs should be testable - each scenario is a potential test case.

## Project: LeaRPcast ??Android Radio & Podcast App

### Identity
- App name: LeaRPcast
- applicationId: LeaRPcast (package root: com.learpc.learpc)
- Status: Brand new project (no existing code)
- Platform: Android (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose)

### Canonical Naming (THIS FILE IS AUTHORITATIVE ??overrides all docs/)
- Application class: `LeaRPcastApplication` (NOT RadioCastApplication)
- Package root: `com.learpc.learpc` (NOT com.example.radiocast)
- Root project name in settings.gradle.kts: `LeaRPcast`
- docs/ reference files use `com.example.radiocast` / `RadioCastApplication` as placeholder names;
  those are historical artifacts and must be overridden by this config in all agent output.

### Tech Stack (FIXED ??do NOT change)
- Language: Kotlin
- UI: Jetpack Compose
- Player core: AndroidX Media3 / ExoPlayer
- Background playback: MediaSessionService
- Media control: MediaSession + MediaController
- Download: Media3 DownloadManager + DownloadService
- Background tasks: WorkManager
- Local DB: Room
- Preferences: DataStore
- Network: Retrofit + OkHttp
- RSS parsing: XmlPullParser (custom FeedParser)
- Radio data source: RadioBrowser API (https://www.radio-browser.info/)
- DI: Hilt
- Concurrency: Coroutines + Flow
- Logging: Timber

### Module Structure (FIXED ??do NOT restructure)
:app, :core:common, :core:ui, :core:network, :core:database,
:core:datastore, :core:media, :core:model, :core:testing,
:domain, :feature:radio, :feature:podcast, :feature:player,
:feature:downloads, :feature:settings

### Key Architecture Rules
- Single ExoPlayer instance in PlaybackService (MediaSessionService)
- UI never directly accesses ExoPlayer or DAOs
- PlaybackStateModel / PlayableItem / InterruptionSnapshot naming is FROZEN
- Repository interfaces live in :domain, implementations in :app/data/repository
- Workers live in :app/work
- PlaybackService lives in :core:media/service

### Reference Documents (in /docs folder)
- radio_podcast_android_prd.md ??PRD + MVP scope
- radio_podcast_technical_design_spec_v_1.md ??TDS v1
- radio_podcast_data_schema_v_1.md ??Data Schema v1
- radio_podcast_project_structure_v_1.md ??Project Structure Spec v1
- radio_podcast_issue_list_v_1.md ??Issue List v1
- radio_podcast_ai_agent_execution_pack_v_1.md ??AI Agent Execution Pack v1

### Agent Rules
- One issue per change (unless explicitly batched)
- Always output pre-implementation understanding first
- Never self-modify schema, module structure, or frozen naming
- Always include handoff summary for next agent
- ALWAYS use canonical naming from this file, NEVER copy class/package names from docs/ verbatim

### UI String Management (MANDATORY)
- App shell UI strings MUST be defined in `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`
- Feature-specific UI strings MUST be defined in the owning feature module's `src/main/res/values/strings.xml`
- The owning module is the module that renders the UI surface for that string
- The strings.xml files MUST use UTF-8 encoding (declared as `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>`)
- NO hardcoded string literals are allowed in Composable functions
- Use `stringResource(R.string.key_name)` in Compose UI
- String key naming: snake_case, prefixed by screen/component
  (e.g., `radio_screen_reconnecting`, `player_pause_button`)
- Plurals and format strings must also live in strings.xml
- This rule applies to ALL agents across ALL issues
